info.title: Edda
info.description: The services behind Edda: auth, characters, combat and monsters. Behind the HTTPS proxy they share one address; run on their own, each has its own (see docs/api.md). Every route but a few needs a token from `POST /login`.

Campaign.description: A campaign: its id, name and edition.

edition.description: Chosen when the campaign is created.

Challenge.description: `POST /login/challenge`: what to sign to log in, valid for a minute.

server.description:
The auth service's own key, which the device should check against
the one it expects (so it isn't logging in somewhere else).

campaign.description: The campaign it belongs to; only that campaign's devices can see it.

owners.description:
The player devices that play it, by key (as `auth devices` shows
them): they may change it, and act for it in a fight. The DM's
devices may change any character.

version.description:
Incremented on every change. Send it back in `If-Match` when replacing
the sheet so stale copies can't overwrite newer data.

Character.description: A stored character: server-assigned metadata plus the editable sheet.

oneOf.description:
Cast a known spell, expending the appropriate slot. Cantrips and
ritual casts don't use a slot.

at_level.description: Slot level to cast at (upcasting). Defaults to the spell's level.

pact.description: Use a Pact Magic slot instead of a regular one.

ritual.description: Cast as a ritual (spell must have the ritual tag).

CharacterAction.description:
A change made in play, applied atomically by the character service:
`POST /characters/{id}/actions`.

CharacterSheet.description:
The editable contents of a character sheet. This is the request body for
both creating and replacing a character.

resources.description: Limited-use class features and abilities (Action Surge, Rage, Ki...).

CharacterSummary.description: Lightweight view used when listing characters.

owners.description: The player devices that play it, by key.

Claims.description: What a token grants: who is calling, in which campaign, as what.

edition.description: The rules the campaign plays by, so services can apply them.

name.description: "Vex's laptop", or the service's name. Used as the actor in logs.

ClassLevel.description: Levels in one class (with its subclass, and the ability it casts with, if any).

oneOf.description: Set for classes that cast spells (e.g. Intelligence for Wizard).

ClientMessage.description: Sent by a client over a combat's WebSocket.

oneOf.description:
Join the combat, at any point. If `initiative` is already set the
combatant slots straight into the turn order.

Add `count` of a monster from the campaign's monsters, named and
numbered on from any already in the fight ("Goblin 3"), at their
maximum hit points or, with `roll`, rolled. Only the server can
decide this (it needs the stat block and dice); see
[`super::add_monsters`].

Roll d20 + modifier. Pass `roll` when the player rolled physical
dice; leave it out to have the server roll.
Server rolls for everyone who hasn't got initiative yet.

Record a spell cast in the log. The slot is spent on the caster's
character sheet, separately; `slot` says which, for the record.
For a concentration spell, `concentration` is the id of the effect
that puts it into play on its targets (ending the caster's previous
concentration).

Use a limited feature (Rage, Action Surge...). For a character, the
combat service spends the uses on their sheet first.

Interrupt an active combat. While paused, only `Resume` and `End`
are accepted.

Take back one of the sender's own earlier commands: `command`, or
when that's left out, their latest one not yet undone. Only the
server can decide this (it needs the log); see [`super::undo`].

CombatCommand.description: What a participant wants to happen. Turned into events by [`decide`].

oneOf.description: A record only: the slot was spent on the caster's sheet.

A record; the combat service spends the use on the character's
sheet before logging it.

The command `command` was undone. The events after it, from the
same undo, put back what that command changed.

A combatant put back as they were (or with their own command's
change reverted), joining again if they had left.
An effect put back, in play again if it had ended.
Status, round and turn set back.

CombatEvent.description:
Something that happened in a combat. Events are facts: they carry
outcomes (the rolled number, the resulting HP) so replaying the log never
needs to re-roll or re-decide anything.

CombatSnapshot.description: The current state of a combat as of log position `seq`.

CombatState.description: Where a combat stands: the result of applying its log, event by event.

campaign.description: The campaign this combat belongs to.

combatants.description: Always kept in initiative order; combatants without initiative last.

CombatStatus.description: Whether a combat is being set up, running, paused or over.

Combatant.description: Anyone in a combat: a character, a monster, or anyone else the DM adds.

character_id.description: Set when this combatant is a character from the character service.

concealed.description:
Its hit points and armor class are behind the DM's screen: a
player's device sees monsters like this (see [`view`]).

hit_points.description: While [`Self::concealed`], only how hurt it looks: see [`Vitality`].

id.description:
Chosen by the client that adds the combatant, so it can predict the
outcome exactly. The server rejects duplicates.

initiative.description: Initiative total. `None` until rolled or set.

monster_id.description:
Set when this combatant is a monster from the monster service, so
its stat block can be shown.

CommandEnvelope.description:
A command plus the metadata that makes it trackable. `command_id` is
chosen by the client: the server tags the resulting events with it (so
the client knows its prediction was confirmed) and ignores repeats (so
resending after a dropped connection is safe).

actor.description: Free-text name of whoever issued it, for the log ("DM", "Travis").

ConditionText.description: A condition, such as Prone, or any other named effect worth describing.

Device.description:
A device of a campaign: its certificate, and when it was added and
revoked.

DeviceCert.description:
A statement that `device` belongs to `campaign` with `role`, signed by
`issuer`: a DM device of that campaign, or for the very first DM device
(set up with a one-time code) the device itself.

issued_at.description: Whole seconds since 1970, so the signed encoding is a plain integer.

name.description: Whose device it is, for people: "Vex's laptop".

Edition.description: Which rules a campaign plays by: the 2014 or the 2024 ones.

Effect.description: Anything in play with a duration or a target: spells, conditions, auras.

concentration.description:
A creature can concentrate on one effect at a time, and loses
concentration when dropped to 0 HP.

oneOf.description: `None` lasts until removed.

Encounter.description: A stored plan: server-assigned metadata plus the plan itself.

EncounterPlan.description:
A fight planned ahead: its monsters, who of the party it's for, and
notes.

party.description: The characters it's balanced for; empty means the whole party.

allOf.description: A condition, such as Prone, or any other named effect worth describing.

campaign.description: The campaign whose homebrew it is; `None` for the shared library.

Entry_ConditionText.description: A stored piece of rules text: server-assigned metadata plus the text.

allOf.description:
A spell as the books describe it. Everything but the name has a
default, so a homebrew spell needs only what it has.

description.description:
Paragraphs, one per line; `- ` starts a list item and `**…**` is
bold.

higher_levels.description: Casting it with a higher slot (or, for a cantrip, at higher levels).

campaign.description: The campaign whose homebrew it is; `None` for the shared library.

Entry_SpellText.description: A stored piece of rules text: server-assigned metadata plus the text.

Expiry.description:
When an effect ends: at the start of `at_turn_of`'s turn in `round`, or
at the start of `round` if there's no such combatant (5e durations run
from the caster's turn; for an effect nobody cast, from the turn it was
put down in).

Feature.description: A trait, action, reaction or legendary action.

HitPoints.description: Current, maximum and temporary hit points.

LoggedEvent.description: One entry in a combat's permanent log.

command_id.description: The command that caused it; `None` for the `Created` event.

seq.description: Position in the log, starting at 1 with no gaps.

campaign.description:
The campaign whose homebrew it is; `None` for the shared library,
which every campaign (of a matching edition) sees.

Monster.description: A stored monster: server-assigned metadata plus the stat block.

MonsterSheet.description:
A full stat block. Everything but the name has a default, so a file
needs only what the monster actually has.

armor.description: What the AC comes from: "leather armor, shield".

oneOf.description: The rules it's written for; `None` suits either.

hit_dice.description: The hit dice, e.g. "2d6" or "18d10+36"; empty if there are none.

initiative.description: Overrides the Dexterity modifier (2024 stat blocks print it).

saving_throws.description: Saving throw bonuses that differ from the plain modifier.

max_hit_points.description: What its hit dice can come to at most, which it joins a fight with.

shared.description: In the shared library rather than the campaign's own.

xp.description:
Experience points, from its challenge rating if the stat block
doesn't say.

NewCombat.description: `POST /combats`: a name, a plan, or both.

encounter.description: A planned encounter to start it from, with the plan's monsters in it.

name.description: What to call it; with a plan, the plan's name by default.

NewEffect.description: An effect for a command to put into play.

id.description: Chosen by the client, like combatant ids.

rounds.description:
Duration in rounds, counted in turns of the source, or (with no
source, like a fire on the floor) of whoever's turn it is when it's
added; `None` lasts until removed. Targets are optional too.

Nonce.description: 32 random bytes, for challenges. Shown as unpadded base64url.

slot_level.description: All pact slots are this level (1-5).

PactMagic.description: Warlock Pact Magic: slots all of one level.

PairingMessage.description:
A message relayed between the two sides of a pairing:
`PUT`/`GET /pairings/{slot}/{host|joiner}/{n}`. Opaque to the server.

PairingSlot.description: `POST /pairings` (DM only): a slot for pairing a new device.

name.description: Its name when planned, shown even if it's since been deleted.

roll.description: Roll their hit points when the fight starts, instead of the maximum.

Pool.description: A count of limited uses: spell slots, Action Surge, Ki points, etc.

Principal.description: Who a token is for: a DM device, a player's, or a service.

PublicKey.description: An Ed25519 public key. Shown as unpadded base64url.

Recharge.description: When a resource comes back on its own.

Resource.description: A named, limited-use class feature or ability, e.g. Action Surge.

RestKind.description: A short or a long rest.

Role.description: What a device may do in its campaign.

ServerKey.description: `GET /public-key`: the key tokens are signed with.

oneOf.description: Sent on connect, and again if this client fell too far behind.

data.description: Sent on connect, and again if this client fell too far behind.

oneOf.description: Broadcast to everyone, in log order.

data.description: Broadcast to everyone, in log order.

oneOf.description: Sent only to the client whose command was refused.

data.description: Sent only to the client whose command was refused.

oneOf.description:
The command was already applied earlier (e.g. resent after a
reconnect); its events are already part of the state.

data.description:
The command was already applied earlier (e.g. resent after a
reconnect); its events are already part of the state.

ServerMessage.description: Sent by the server over a combat's WebSocket.

Session.description: `POST /login`: a token, and what it says.

SetupRequest.description:
`POST /setup`: the first DM device of a campaign, with the one-time code
printed when the campaign was created.

Signature.description: An Ed25519 signature. Shown as unpadded base64url.

Spell.description: A spell the character knows or has prepared.

class.description: Which class grants this spell, for multiclass characters.

prepared.description:
Whether the spell can currently be cast. Defaults to true so "known"
casters (Sorcerer, Bard, ...) needn't care; Wizards and Clerics toggle it.

SpellSlot.description:
The slot a spell was cast with: a regular slot of some level, or a
Pact Magic slot (whose level is fixed).

SpellText.description:
A spell as the books describe it. Everything but the name has a
default, so a homebrew spell needs only what it has.

description.description:
Paragraphs, one per line; `- ` starts a list item and `**…**` is
bold.

higher_levels.description: Casting it with a higher slot (or, for a cantrip, at higher levels).

Spellcasting.description: Everything about a character's spellcasting. Empty for non-casters.

oneOf.description: Warlock Pact Magic slots. Recover on a short or long rest.

slots.description: Regular spell slots keyed by slot level (1-9). Recover on a long rest.

Stale.description: A `412`: the character as it is now, to re-apply a change to.

token.description: From the auth service's `POST /login`; valid for 15 minutes.
